title: John Calvin
source: Public domain. Consolidated from John Calvin, Commentary on the Epistles to the Corinthians, translated by John Pringle, Calvin Translation Society, and the Institutes of the Christian Religion, translated by Henry Beveridge; both as published by the Christian Classics Ethereal Library.
body: John Calvin on Second Corinthians, chapter 12. In his Commentary on the Epistles to the Corinthians, in the John Pringle translation, Calvin writes at Second Corinthians 12, verse 1: It is not expedient for me to glory Now, when as it were in the middle of the course, he restrains himself from proceeding farther, and in this way he most appropriately reproves the impudence of his rivals and declares that it is with reluctance, that he engages in this sort of contest with them. In the Institutes of the Christian Religion, in the Henry Beveridge translation, Calvin draws on this chapter again in Book 3, chapter 3.
